title: With default fonts and certain specific panel thicknesses, the time display bounces a bit when any digits display a 4
line: The Digital Clock's time no longer shrinks on vertical panels or shifts sideways in its tooltip when it ends in a 4.
explanation: Qt adds a trailing glyph's overhang to a text's width, and in Noto Sans a final 4 overhangs its advance, so for that second the time was about a pixel wider even with tabular digits. On vertical panels the time label used Text.Fit on its live text, so its font shrank a pixel; in the tooltip (duplicate 519039) the time zone grid is centered, so the wider time column moved the whole line one pixel to the left. The vertical panel label now uses Text.VerticalFit, whose height already comes from sizehelper's widest-digit string, and the tooltip's time column takes its width from the text's advance (TextMetrics.advanceWidth), which does not change with the digits.

commits.message:
applets/digital-clock: keep the time steady when it shows a 4

A trailing 4 overhangs its advance, so for that second vertical panels
shrank the time's font and the tooltip's centered time zone grid moved.
Fit the panel time to its height only and size tooltip times by advance.

BUG: 509556

patches.diff:
From b28945bf41bdd92f87f444f8fdefc7677908b627 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 02:31:05 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/digital-clock: keep the time steady when it shows a 4

A trailing 4 overhangs its advance, so for that second vertical panels
shrank the time's font and the tooltip's centered time zone grid moved.
Fit the panel time to its height only and size tooltip times by advance.

BUG: 509556
---
 applets/digital-clock/DigitalClock.qml | 2 +-
 applets/digital-clock/Tooltip.qml      | 7 +++++++
 2 files changed, 8 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applets/digital-clock/DigitalClock.qml b/applets/digital-clock/DigitalClock.qml
index 8c918109d0..0d4b38b55c 100644
--- a/applets/digital-clock/DigitalClock.qml
+++ b/applets/digital-clock/DigitalClock.qml
@@ -266,7 +266,7 @@ MouseArea {
                 timeLabel.height: sizehelper.contentHeight
                 timeLabel.width: main.width
                 timeLabel.font.pixelSize: Math.min(timeLabel.height, fontHelper.font.pixelSize)
-                timeLabel.fontSizeMode: Text.Fit
+                timeLabel.fontSizeMode: Text.VerticalFit
 
                 timeZoneLabel.height: Math.max(0.7 * timeLabel.height, dateLabel.minimumPixelSize)
                 timeZoneLabel.width: main.width
diff --git a/applets/digital-clock/Tooltip.qml b/applets/digital-clock/Tooltip.qml
index 7ecafd0baf..c05e1666fd 100644
--- a/applets/digital-clock/Tooltip.qml
+++ b/applets/digital-clock/Tooltip.qml
@@ -147,6 +147,8 @@ Item {
 
                     // Layout.fillWidth is buggy here
                     Layout.alignment: index % 2 === 0 ? Qt.AlignRight : Qt.AlignLeft
+                    // The implicit width grows when the last glyph overhangs, e.g. a 4, which shifts the centered grid
+                    Layout.preferredWidth: index % 2 === 1 ? timeMetrics.advanceWidth : -1
                     text: index % 2 === 0
                         ? i18nc("@label %1 is a city or time zone name", "%1:", tzLabel)
                         : formatTime(tzClock.dateTime, Plasmoid.configuration.showSeconds > 0) + formatOffset(tzClock.dateTime)
@@ -155,6 +157,11 @@ Item {
                         timeZone: label.modelData
                         trackSeconds: Plasmoid.configuration.showSeconds
                     }
+                    TextMetrics {
+                        id: timeMetrics
+                        font: label.font
+                        text: label.text
+                    }
 
                     textFormat: Text.PlainText
 
--

media.caption: Master, 60 px left panel, 24h with seconds: :04 and :14 are drawn smaller than :03, :05 and :15
Fixed: :04 and :54 are the same size as their neighbours
Master, hover tooltip at scale 2 with seconds (duplicate 519039): at :14 the whole time zone line sits one pixel left of the red line
Fixed: at :44 the line stays on the red line like :43 and :45

review.text: Fixes the exact root cause of the vertical-panel clock bounce by switching timeLabel.fontSizeMode from Text.Fit to Text.VerticalFit, matching the oneLineDate state. Because sizehelper already computes the height that fits the widest time string into main.width, fitting only vertically prevents trailing-4 glyph overhang from shrinking the font for a single second. Before/after screenshots and multi-width/12h verification confirm the fix with no regressions.

reviews.text: Fixes the exact root cause of the vertical-panel clock bounce by switching timeLabel.fontSizeMode from Text.Fit to Text.VerticalFit, matching the oneLineDate state. Because sizehelper already computes the height that fits the widest time string into main.width, fitting only vertically prevents trailing-4 glyph overhang from shrinking the font for a single second. Before/after screenshots and multi-width/12h verification confirm the fix with no regressions.

My earlier request is resolved. The duplicate 519039 tooltip case was tested on master and does reproduce at scale 2 with the UTC-offset label: the line moves 1 logical px at :x4. The commit now gives the tooltip's time column a width from TextMetrics.advanceWidth, which stays constant with tnum digits, and the label is NoWrap/ElideNone, so nothing gets elided or wrapped. before-2/after-2 show the centered line staying on the reference across :x4, and the earlier Text.VerticalFit change still fixes the vertical-panel shrink. With ffe832ee60 already covering the horizontal case, BUG: 509556 closes the report and its duplicate.

history.text: Switching the vertical-panel timeLabel from Text.Fit to Text.VerticalFit is the right minimal fix: sizehelper already fits the widest-digit time string to the panel width, so the font no longer depends on the live digits, and the before/after strips clearly show :04/:14/:54 no longer shrinking. The horizontal 40 px case was already fixed by ffe832ee60. However, Nate marked 519039 as a duplicate of this bug, and it reports a different surface: in the hover tooltip the 4 pushes the second line sideways (6.6.4, after the sizehelper and tnum fixes). That case was not tested with a 24h clock ending in 4 and is not touched by the patch, so BUG: 509556 would close it unverified.
changes: Test the duplicate 519039 case on master (hover tooltip, 24h, seconds shown, across :x4); if the second line still shifts, fix it too (e.g. stable width for the tooltip's time line), otherwise record in verify that it no longer reproduces

history.summary: The tooltip case from duplicate 519039 still happened on master and is now fixed in the same commit: the tooltip's time column takes its width from the text's advance, so a trailing 4 no longer moves the centered time zone line. Commit message, explanation, verify and media updated.

answers.request: Test the duplicate 519039 case on master (hover tooltip, 24h, seconds shown, across :x4); if the second line still shifts, fix it too (e.g. stable width for the tooltip's time line), otherwise record in verify that it no longer reproduces
answers.answer: Tested on kdetest6 pure master at scale 2 (2560x1600), 24h, seconds Always: with the time zone shown as UTC offset the whole line moves 1 logical px left at :14 and :24 (with CET or the city name the half-pixel change rounds away, which is why it looked fine at first). Cause: Qt adds the trailing 4's overhang to the label's implicit width, and the grid is centered. Fixed in Tooltip.qml by setting the time column's Layout.preferredWidth to TextMetrics.advanceWidth; after the fix the line stays put across :44 and :54 (before-2/after-2), and multi-zone, offset and 12h tooltips still lay out correctly.
